items.stem: If the distance between the points (3, −5) and (x, −5) is 15 units, then the values of x are:
items.answer: Both points share the ordinate −5, so the distance reduces to the horizontal gap: 15² = (x − 3)², giving x − 3 = ±15. Hence x = 18 or x = −12, i.e. the values are −12 and 18.

items.stem: AD is a median of ΔABC with vertices A(5, −6), B(6, 4) and C(0, 0). Length AD is equal to :
items.answer: A median runs to the mid-point of the opposite side, so D is the mid-point of BC: D = ((6 + 0)/2, (4 + 0)/2) = (3, 2). Then AD = √((3 − 5)² + (2 − (−6))²) = √(4 + 64) = √68 units.

items.stem: The centre of a circle is at (2, 0). If one end of a diameter is at (6, 0), then the other end is at
items.answer: The centre is the mid-point of a diameter. With the far end (x, y): (x + 6)/2 = 2 gives x = −2, and (y + 0)/2 = 0 gives y = 0. The other end is (−2, 0).

items.stem: The distance of the point (−6, 8) from x-axis is
items.answer: Distance from the x-axis is the absolute value of the ordinate. Here |y| = |8| = 8, so the point stands 8 units from the x-axis.
items.ocr: The printed solution mis-words itself - it says 'distance from the y-axis is the absolute value of its x-coordinate, which is 8', but |x| = 6, not 8. The number it reports (8) and the printed key (c) are both right for the question as asked (distance from the x-axis = |y| = 8), so the key is not contradicted; only the prose is wrong. Answer rewritten correctly.

items.stem: The point of intersection of the line represented by 3x − y = 3 and y-axis is given by
items.answer: Every point of the y-axis has x = 0. Substituting x = 0 into 3x − y = 3 gives −y = 3, so y = −3. The line meets the y-axis at (0, −3).

items.stem: The centroid of the triangle whose vertices are (3, −7), (−8, 6) and (5, 10) is
items.answer: The centroid averages the three vertices: x = (3 − 8 + 5)/3 = 0/3 = 0 and y = (−7 + 6 + 10)/3 = 9/3 = 3. The centroid is (0, 3).

items.stem: The ratio in which the point (2, y) divides the join of (−4, 3) and (6, 3), hence the value of y is
items.answer: Take the ratio as k : 1. Then 2 = (6k − 4)/(k + 1), so 2k + 2 = 6k − 4 and k = 3/2, i.e. the ratio 3 : 2. Both given points have ordinate 3, and indeed y = (3·3 + 2·3)/(3 + 2) = 3. So the ratio is 3 : 2 with y = 3.

items.stem: The point P on x-axis equidistant from the points A(−1, 0) and B(5, 0) is
items.answer: Let P = (x, 0). Setting PA² = PB² gives (x + 1)² = (5 − x)², so x² + 2x + 1 = 25 − 10x + x², hence 12x = 24 and x = 2. Since A and B both lie on the x-axis, P is simply their mid-point, (2, 0).

items.stem: The co-ordinates of the point which is reflection of point (−3, 5) in x-axis are
items.answer: Reflecting in the x-axis keeps the abscissa and reverses the sign of the ordinate. So (−3, 5) maps to (−3, −5).
items.ocr: The book prints a graph beside the solution showing (−3, 5) and (−3, −5); it is a solution figure, not needed to read the question, so it is not attached.

items.stem: If the point P (6, 2) divides the line segment joining A(6, 5) and B(4, y) in the ratio 3 : 1 then the value of y is
items.answer: By the section formula on the ordinates, 2 = (3y + 1·5)/(3 + 1) = (3y + 5)/4. So 3y + 5 = 8, giving 3y = 3 and y = 1.

items.stem: The distance between the points (a cos θ + b sin θ, 0), and (0, a sin θ − b cos θ) is
items.answer: d² = (a cos θ + b sin θ)² + (a sin θ − b cos θ)². Expanding, the cross terms +2ab cos θ sin θ and −2ab sin θ cos θ cancel, leaving a²(cos²θ + sin²θ) + b²(sin²θ + cos²θ) = a² + b². Hence d = √(a² + b²).

items.stem: If the point P(k, 0) divides the line segment joining the points A(2, −2) and B(−7, 4) in the ratio 1 : 2, then the value of k is
The coordinates of a point A on y-axis, at a distance of 4 units from x-axis and below it are
items.answer: A point on the y-axis has abscissa 0. Being 4 units below the x-axis makes the ordinate −4. So A is (0, −4).

items.stem: The distance of the point (−12, 5) from the origin is
items.answer: Distance from the origin is √(x² + y²) = √((−12)² + 5²) = √(144 + 25) = √169 = 13 units.
items.ocr: No board/year tag is printed against this solution.

items.stem: Distance of point P(3, 4) from x-axis is
items.answer: Distance from the x-axis equals the absolute value of the ordinate, |4| = 4 units. (Its distance from the y-axis would be |3| = 3 units.)
items.ocr: Option (d) is printed as '1 units'; kept as printed. The graph beside the solution is a solution figure, not attached.

items.stem: The distance of the point P(−3, −4) from the x-axis (in units) is
items.answer: Distance from the x-axis is |y| = |−4| = 4 units.

items.stem: If A(m/3, 5) is the mid-point of the line segment joining the points Q(−6, 7) and R(−2, 3), then the value of m is
items.answer: The mid-point of QR is ((−6 − 2)/2, (7 + 3)/2) = (−4, 5). Equating abscissae, m/3 = −4, so m = −12.
items.ocr: Stem is printed at the foot of book page 273 (image p042); its options and solution run over onto book page 274 (image p003).

items.stem: The mid-point of the line-segment AB is P(0, 4), if the coordinates of B are (−2, 3) then the co-ordinates of A are
items.answer: Let A = (x, y). From the mid-point formula, (x − 2)/2 = 0 gives x = 2, and (y + 3)/2 = 4 gives y = 5. So A is (2, 5).

items.stem: x-axis divides the line segment joining A(2, −3) and B(5, 6) in the ratio
items.answer: A point of the x-axis has ordinate 0. Writing the ratio as k : 1, 0 = (6k − 3)/(k + 1), so 6k = 3 and k = 1/2. The ratio is therefore 1 : 2.

items.stem: The point which divides the line segment joining the points (8, −9) and (2, 3) in the ratio 1 : 2 internally lies in the
items.answer: By the section formula, x = (1·2 + 2·8)/3 = 18/3 = 6 and y = (1·3 + 2·(−9))/3 = −15/3 = −5. The point (6, −5) has a positive abscissa and a negative ordinate, so it lies in the IV quadrant.

items.stem: If the centre of a circle is (3, 5) and end points of a diameter are (4, 7) and (2, y), then the value of y is
items.answer: The centre is the mid-point of the diameter, so 5 = (7 + y)/2. Hence 7 + y = 10 and y = 3.

items.stem: If the distance between the points A(4, p) and B(1, 0) is 5 units then the value(s) of p is(are)
items.answer: 5 = √((1 − 4)² + (0 − p)²) gives 25 = 9 + p², so p² = 16 and p = ±4. Both signs satisfy the distance, so p = ±4.

items.stem: If the points A(4, 3) and B(x, 5) are on the circle with centre O(2, 3), then the value of x is
items.answer: Both points lie on the circle, so OA = OB. Then √((4 − 2)² + 0²) = √((x − 2)² + (5 − 3)²) gives 4 = (x − 2)² + 4, so (x − 2)² = 0 and x = 2.

items.stem: The point on the x-axis which is equidistant from the points A(−2, 3) and B(5, 4) is
items.answer: Let P = (x, 0) with AP = BP. Then (x + 2)² + 9 = (x − 5)² + 16, so x² + 4x + 13 = x² − 10x + 41, giving 14x = 28 and x = 2. The point is (2, 0).

items.stem: C is the mid-point of PQ, if P is (4, x), C is (y, −1) and Q is (−2, 4), then x and y respectively are
items.answer: From the mid-point formula on abscissae, y = (4 − 2)/2 = 1. On ordinates, (x + 4)/2 = −1 gives x + 4 = −2, so x = −6. Hence x = −6 and y = 1.

items.stem: If x − 2y + k = 0 is a median of the triangle whose vertices are at points A(−1, 3), B(0, 4) and C(−5, 2), then the value of k is
items.answer: Every median passes through the centroid, which is G = ((−1 + 0 − 5)/3, (3 + 4 + 2)/3) = (−2, 3). Substituting into x − 2y + k = 0 gives −2 − 6 + k = 0, so k = 8.
items.ocr: The printed working shows the centroid's abscissa as (−1 + 0 − 5)/2 - a typo for /3; the value it then reports, (−2, 3), is the correct /3 result, and the key (d) follows from it.

items.stem: In the given figure, the area of ΔABC (in sq units) is
items.answer: The figure gives A(1, 3), B(−1, 0) and C(4, 0). BC lies along the x-axis with length 4 − (−1) = 5, and the height from A is its ordinate 3. So the area is ½ × 5 × 3 = 7.5 sq units.
items.ocr: The vertices are shown only on the printed graph, not stated in words, so the figure is required.

items.stem: The distance of the point P(2, 3) from the x-axis is
items.answer: For a point (x, y), the perpendicular distance from the x-axis is |y|. Here it is 3.

items.stem: The distance between the points A(0, 6) and B(0, −2) is
items.answer: Both points lie on the y-axis, so AB = √((0 − 0)² + (−2 − 6)²) = √64 = 8.

items.stem: The distance of the point P(−6, 8) from the origin is
items.answer: Distance from the origin is √(x² + y²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10.

items.stem: The distance between the points (0, 5) and (−5, 0) is
If AOBC is a rectangle whose three vertices are A(0, 3), O(0, 0) and B(5, 0), then the length of its diagonal is
items.answer: A diagonal joins A(0, 3) to B(5, 0), so its length is √((5 − 0)² + (0 − 3)²) = √(25 + 9) = √34.
items.ocr: A sketch of the rectangle is printed with the question, but every vertex it needs is already given in words, so the figure is not required.

items.stem: The perimeter of a triangle with vertices (0, 4), (0, 0) and (3, 0) is
items.answer: Call the vertices A(0, 4), O(0, 0) and B(3, 0). Then OA = 4, OB = 3 and AB = √(3² + 4²) = 5. The perimeter is 4 + 3 + 5 = 12.
items.ocr: A sketch is printed between the stem and the options, but all three vertices are stated in the stem, so the figure is not required.

items.stem: The point which lies on the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining the points A(−2, −5) and B(2, 5) is
items.answer: A perpendicular bisector always passes through the mid-point of the segment. The mid-point of AB is ((−2 + 2)/2, (−5 + 5)/2) = (0, 0), so (0, 0) lies on it.

items.stem: If the point P(2, 1) lies on the line segment joining points A(4, 2) and B(8, 4), then
items.answer: The three points are collinear on y = x/2. Measuring along it, AP = √((4 − 2)² + (2 − 1)²) = √5 and AB = √((8 − 4)² + (4 − 2)²) = 2√5. Hence AP = ½ AB.
items.ocr: As printed, P(2, 1) is not between A and B - it lies outside the segment AB on the same line. The printed solution treats A as the dividing point and reaches m : n = 1 : 2, from which AP = ½ AB; that result is what the distances confirm, so the key (d) stands.

items.stem: If P(a/3, 4) is the mid-point of the line segment joining the points Q(−6, 5) and R(−2, 3), then the value of a is
items.answer: The mid-point of QR is ((−6 − 2)/2, (5 + 3)/2) = (−4, 4). Equating abscissae, a/3 = −4, so a = −12.

items.stem: The perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining the points A(1, 5) and B(4, 6) cuts the y-axis at
items.answer: Let P(0, b) be the point where it meets the y-axis. Any point of the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from A and B, so PA² = PB²: 1 + (b − 5)² = 16 + (b − 6)². Expanding, 1 + b² − 10b + 25 = 16 + b² − 12b + 36, so 2b = 26 and b = 13. The point is (0, 13).

items.answer: Apply the distance formula the reason states: PQ² = 100 gives (10 − 2)² + (y + 3)² = 100, so (y + 3)² = 36 and y + 3 = ±6, i.e. y = 3 or y = −9. Neither value is 6, so the assertion is false while the reason is a correct statement of the distance formula.
items.ocr: The printed key reads 'Thus (s) is correct option' - there is no option (s). The worked solution ends 'Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true', which is option (d), so the solution decides it and the key is recorded as D.
